title: Priyank Kharge shares AI-generated photo linking Bihar cartridge accused to RSS
excerpt: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge has been called out for spreading fake news after using a misleading, AI-manipulated photograph to suggest that all four accused in the Bihar-Haryana ammunition-smuggling case were associated with the RSS. The original photograph tells a different story, exposing how an altered image was used to push a political narrative without verifying the facts. The controversy concerns the seizure of 44,250 live cartridges in two separate operations in Bihar and Haryana. Following the arrests, a photograph showing several men in RSS uniforms began circulating on social media, with claims that all four accused in the Bihar case were members of the organisation. Kharge used the alleged RSS connection to question the BJP and the RSS, demanding answers about the accused, their organisational positions and their possible involvement in the ammunition racket. The massive seizure of 44,250 live cartridges in Bihar and Haryana has exposed a serious interstate ammunition-smuggling network. This is not an ordinary criminal case. This is a grave national security concern. Even more disturbing are reports and photographs allegedly showing… pic.twitter.com/I8yY54X9A8 — Priyank Kharge / ಪ್ರಿಯಾಂಕ್ ಖರ್ಗೆ (@PriyankKharge) November 10, 2026 However, the viral photograph does not show what these claims suggest. The original image has been traced to an Instagram post by Abhishek Tiwari, one of the accused, published on March 29, 2026. The original photograph showed a group of men, but only Abhishek Tiwari was wearing the RSS uniform. The viral version had been altered to make several other individuals appear in the same uniform. The manipulation changed the appearance of faces, clothing and other details, creating a misleading impression that all the accused were associated with the RSS. Fact-check exposes AI manipulation After examining the viral photograph and comparing it with the original image available on Abhishek Tiwari’s Instagram account. The comparison revealed several inconsistencies. Some faces appeared unusually similar, while the placement of sticks and other objects did not match the original photograph. We have a fake news peddler as Home Minister of our state. And this bloke wanted to set up some fact check unit or something. Sad state of affairs. https://t.co/COI2pMtmsG pic.twitter.com/FxQdsxIpve — Tejasvi Surya (@Tejasvi_Surya) November 10, 2026 The original photograph, posted on March 29, showed only Abhishek Tiwari wearing the RSS uniform. The other individuals were not dressed in the same manner as they appeared in the viral version. The findings expose how an altered photograph was used to give credibility to a political claim. The ammunition-smuggling investigation is real, but the viral image cannot be treated as evidence that all four accused were RSS members. What is the 44,250-cartridge case? The controversy began after police operations in Bihar and Haryana led to the recovery of 44,250 live cartridges. The seizures were made in separate investigations into suspected interstate ammunition smuggling. The combined recovery included 19,250 cartridges in Bihar and 25,000 in Haryana. Bihar: Three arrested in Bhojpur On November 2, Bihar Police and the Special Task Force (STF) arrested three alleged ammunition smugglers during a joint operation near Kulharia Toll Plaza in Bhojpur district. The police recovered 19,250 live cartridges of different calibres and a country-made pistol from their vehicle. The arrested individuals were identified as Chandan Tiwari (26), Saras Kumar (27) and Laltu Kumar (38). Police said the accused could not produce valid documents for the ammunition. Investigators subsequently began examining the source of the cartridges, their intended recipients and the possible involvement of other people in the supply network. Haryana: 25,000 cartridges seized In a separate operation on November 3, Haryana Police’s Special Task Force recovered another 25,000 live cartridges near Rohad in Jhajjar district. Five people from Uttar Pradesh’s Badaun district were initially arrested. A sixth person was subsequently arrested in Sirsa following questioning. The ammunition was recovered from two vehicles. These included 24,400 cartridges from a Tata Harrier and another 600 from a Hyundai Aura. Investigators identified Afifuddin alias Munna Khan, who allegedly operated Badaun Gun House, as a key link in the suspected network. Vijay Goel, who operates a gun house in Sirsa, also came under investigation over his alleged role in supplying the ammunition. Police suspected that the cartridges were being diverted through licensed arms dealers and supplied to illegal arms manufacturers and criminal networks. The investigation also examined markings on the recovered cartridges, including those associated with the Khadki ammunition factory in Pune. Investigators are looking into how ammunition manufactured for authorised purposes allegedly entered illegal channels. Tejasvi Surya calls out Kharge over fake news BJP MP Tejasvi Surya strongly criticised Kharge over the controversy. Reacting to the allegations, Surya accused the Karnataka Home Minister of spreading fake news and questioned his credibility, particularly in light of his earlier proposal to establish a fact-checking unit. Why is Priyank Kharge targeting the RSS? Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge has used the ammunition-smuggling case to launch yet another attack on the RSS. Kharge’s attempt to drag the organisation into the controversy raises an important question: Why is he so determined to target the RSS, even when the photograph being used to suggest a wider organisational connection has been exposed as AI-manipulated? In his post on X, Kharge raised five questions, demanding answers from the RSS and BJP. He questioned whether the accused were RSS Swayamsevaks, what positions they held, where the ammunition was headed, how government-manufactured cartridges entered the illegal market and why the organisation had not responded to the allegations. He also demanded the formal registration of the RSS, arguing that membership records would make the organisation more accountable. Addressing RSS Sarsanghchalak Dr Mohan Bhagwat, he even offered to facilitate the registration and pay the fees himself. But Kharge’s repeated attempts to make the RSS the centre of a criminal investigation deserve scrutiny of their own. The RSS is a voluntary organisation with a long history of social and community service, disaster relief, educational initiatives and grassroots activities. title: Invest Telangana Summit to feature six expos, 52 sessions
excerpt: Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026, scheduled to be held next month, will feature six expos, 52 sector sessions and nine events and pavilions. Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 (ITGS 2026) will be held at Bharat Future City here from December 7 to December 9. Being organised by Invest Telangana under the Industries & Commerce Department, the summit forms part of the Telangana Rising 2047 vision, which aims to make Telangana a 3 trillion US dollar economy by 2047.ITGS 2026 will have six expo hangars, compared with one expo hall in 2025. The total area rises to 72,250 square meters from 27,500 square meters last year. More than 60,000 square meters of exhibition space is proposed across 12 sectors and pavilions. Sessions will follow the journey of an investment in five stages: pledge, plot, plant, payroll and product. The summit will have an inaugural plenary and 52 sector sessions in four parallel halls. The halls are themed Engines of Telangana, The Wider Economy, The Telangana Stack and the Social Sector Forum. Business platforms include a CEOâ€"Minister Deal Floor and a Government-to-Business desk. The valedictory on December 9 will publish a Pledge-to-Product Scorecard, so that commitments made at the summit can be followed in public. The state government on Tuesday opened registrations for ITGS 2026. Delegates can register online on the official Government of Telangana portal, invite-itgs2026.telangana.gov.in. According to an official release, the summit will be held under the leadership of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. A Cabinet Sub-Committee chaired by Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarkais is overseeing preparations. Ministers N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, D. Sridhar Babu and Gaddam Vivek are the members. Curtain raisers were held in Hyderabad on October 24 for the Raksha Expo and in New Delhi on October 29 for the summit. Nine events and pavilions are planned, along with side events. Raksha Expo 2026 covers defence, aerospace, space, internal security, and cyber and AI. It has a 14,400 sq m indoor exhibition with five sector pavilions, an outdoor display and live demonstrations of counter-drone, UAS and robotics systems. DRDO, HAL, BEL, BDL, ECIL, Safran, Tata Advanced Systems, L&T Precision, Bharat Forge and Skyroot Aerospace are among the confirmed participants. There will be an Acrobatic Airshow on the inaugural day â€" December 7. Startup Pavilion will have 136 startups across 9,000 sq m, with nominations from T-Hub, T-Works, RICH and WE Hub. The largest groups are defence, space and aerospace (35 startups) and health, biotech and pharma (30).IndiaJoy 2026 and Creators Corner will be held in two halls, one for business and one for the public. It covers animation, VFX, gaming, comics and extended reality, with a 300-seat esports arena. Pharma & Life Science Expo will feature 60 companies, covering the value chain from drug discovery to global capability centres. Telangana Pavilion will be a state showcase in five zones. It features an Ikat and Bathukamma canopy with a live loom, a 360-degree projection hall and Kakatiya stone craft. Industrial Expo will comprise MSMEs to large industries, including the Shakti Pavilion for women enterprises. Its Agriculture & Allied Sectors Pavilion is themed "Farm to Fork â€" Telangana".Telangana climate conclave will be held on December 8, anchored by the EFS&T Department, on preparing the state for an El Nino year. About 200 scientists, policymakers, practitioners, farmers and community leaders will take part in five thematic sessions. It will close with a Telangana Climate Resilience Agenda for the next one, five and 10 years. Education, Research & Skilling Expo will have 47 participants and pavilions. These include universities, IIT Hyderabad, ISB, BITS, NALSAR, Young India Skills University, and UK and Europe pavilions. There will also be the Telangana Innovation Startup Challenge. Startups and independent innovators can apply at tisc.telangana.gov.in to solve challenges set by government departments. These span agriculture, energy, healthcare, education and public infrastructure, led by solar-powered irrigation.

title: WhatsApp's big plan: AI, digital payments and smarter messaging on cards
excerpt: New Delhi, November 10 (IANS): WhatsApp is preparing to expand its services beyond messaging, with artificial intelligence, digital payments and improved communication features emerging as three key priorities under its new global head, Kunal Shah, who took charge as WhatsApp's global head in June 2026, said on Tuesday. Shah outlined the platform's future roadmap after spending his first four months understanding user expectations and identifying areas where the messaging service could improve. WhatsApp currently has more than three billion users worldwide. In a post on X, Shah said the company's focus would be on helping people maintain closer connections while making everyday activities easier to complete within the application. He described WhatsApp as a shared language used by billions of people, where conversations take place through text messages, voice notes, stickers and video interactions."I think of WhatsApp like a shared language, spoken by 3bn+ people. Sometimes we use words, and sometimes it’s a voice note to a parent, a sticker that ends an argument, or a "that was a fun dinner” at the end of the night. Language is at the heart of everything we as people do. We write letters, tell stories, get things done and make plans for the future. A WhatsApp chat is often where we start," he stated."I’ve spent the last few months listening and understanding what our users want from us and what I heard is simple: help people stay close to those who matter to them, and get more done on WhatsApp. So that's what we'll build," Shah added. The first priority will be to make conversations more expressive and user-friendly. WhatsApp plans to improve features such as voice notes, group chats, stickers and video interactions to reflect changing communication habits. Highlighting the scale of engagement on the platform, Shah said users send more than 10 billion voice messages and over four billion stickers every day. The second major focus will be simplifying financial and everyday transactions. Shah noted that several activities, including paying bills, accessing financial services and staying connected while travelling, often begin with a WhatsApp conversation but require users to switch to other applications to complete them."Too many things start in a chat and end with many more steps somewhere else: paying a bill, borrowing money, staying connected when you travel. Each handoff to another task costs time. We're working with financial services and telecom partners so that finishing something feels as easy as starting it," he noted. Artificial intelligence will form the third pillar of WhatsApp's development strategy. "Third, we want to make this all more efficient with AI. It should quietly find what you need, get things done and make sure you never miss a booking or an appointment. The best technology saves you time, so you can get back to the connections that matter," Shah mentioned.
